economic_context: Economic Context: Inflation: 7.2%. Interest Rate: 6.5%. GDP Growth: 2.1%. Unemployment: 15.8%. Exchange Rate: 3.11 TND/USD.
banks_analyzed: Banque de Tunisie et des Émirats (BTE)
Union Bancaire de Commerce et d'Industrie (UBCI)

scenarios.title: Rising Interest Rates and Inflationary Pressures
scenarios.description: Increasing interest rates and inflationary pressures affecting the Tunisian banking sector
scenarios.trigger: Central Bank of Tunisia raises interest rates to combat inflation

timeline.short_term: 0-6 months: Interest rates rise by 1.5%, inflation increases by 1%
timeline.medium_term: 6-18 months: Loan growth slows, deposit rates increase
timeline.long_term: 18-36 months: Higher borrowing costs affect consumer spending, GDP growth slows

sector_impacts.loan_portfolio_quality: Deterioration in loan quality, increased provisioning
sector_impacts.deposit_growth: Slowing deposit growth, increased competition for deposits

differential_impacts.BIAT: Higher exposure to corporate lending may lead to increased credit risk
differential_impacts.BT: Stronger focus on retail banking may help mitigate impact of rising interest rates
differential_impacts.ATB: Higher dependence on wholesale funding may lead to increased funding costs

metrics.interest_rate_spread: Monitor the difference between lending and deposit rates
metrics.non_performing_loans: Track the percentage of non-performing loans in the sector
metrics.deposit_growth_rate: Monitor the annual growth rate of deposits in the sector
metrics.capital_adequacy_ratio: Track the capital adequacy ratio of banks in the sector

risk_factors: Increased credit risk due to higher borrowing costs
Higher funding costs and reduced net interest margins
opportunities: Diversification of revenue streams through non-interest income
Investment in digital channels to reduce costs and improve efficiency
Focus on high-yield lending segments, such as SMEs and mortgages
Strategic partnerships and collaborations to mitigate risks
recommended_actions: Regularly review and adjust interest rate risk management strategies
Diversify funding sources and reduce dependence on wholesale funding
Enhance credit risk assessment and monitoring
Invest in digital transformation to improve operational efficiency

scenarios.title: Economic Shock Impacting Banking Sector
scenarios.description: Significant economic event affecting all Tunisian banks
scenarios.trigger: Sudden collapse of Tunisia's major phosphate export market, leading to a sharp decline in foreign exchange earnings and a subsequent depreciation of the Tunisian dinar (TND)

timeline.month 1-3: Phosphate export market collapse, TND depreciates by 10% against the USD
timeline.month 4-6: Inflation surges to 9.5%, interest rates rise to 7.5% to combat inflationary pressures
timeline.month 7-9: GDP growth slows to 1.5%, unemployment increases to 17.2%
timeline.month 10-12: Banking sector begins to feel the strain, with non-performing loans (NPLs) increasing by 20%

affected_entities: All Tunisian banks, including state-owned and private banks

sector_impacts.credit quality: Deterioration in credit quality, with increased NPLs and loan defaults
sector_impacts.liquidity: Reduced liquidity, as banks face increased withdrawals and reduced deposits
sector_impacts.capital adequacy: Erosion of capital buffers, as banks struggle to maintain regulatory requirements
sector_impacts.profitability: Reduced profitability, as banks face increased provisioning and write-offs

differential_impacts.BIAT: Higher exposure to government securities, making it more vulnerable to interest rate fluctuations
differential_impacts.BT: Stronger focus on retail banking, making it more resilient to economic shocks
differential_impacts.ATB: Higher exposure to SME lending, making it more vulnerable to credit risk

metrics.NPL ratio: Increase in NPL ratio, as a percentage of total loans
metrics.Capital adequacy ratio: Decrease in capital adequacy ratio, as a percentage of risk-weighted assets
metrics.Return on equity (ROE): Decrease in ROE, as a percentage of net income to shareholder equity
metrics.Foreign exchange reserves: Decrease in foreign exchange reserves, as a percentage of total reserves

risk_factors: Increased credit risk due to rising unemployment
Reduced lending appetite due to high interest rates
Depreciation of Tunisian Dinar affecting foreign currency-denominated assets
opportunities: Diversification of revenue streams through non-interest income
Investment in digital channels to reduce costs and improve efficiency
Consolidation and M&A opportunities in a distressed market
recommended_actions: Stress testing and scenario analysis to assess resilience
Diversification of funding sources to reduce dependence on wholesale funding
Enhanced risk management and provisioning for potential losses

scenarios.title: Industry-wide Digital Banking Innovation
scenarios.description: Wave of new digital banking products across multiple banks
scenarios.trigger: Government's announcement of a National Digital Transformation Plan, allocating 100 million TND to support the development of digital infrastructure and encouraging banks to invest in fintech

timeline.short_term: 0-6 months: Banks begin developing digital products and services, partnering with fintech startups and investing in digital infrastructure
timeline.medium_term: 6-18 months: First wave of digital banking products launched, focusing on mobile payment systems and online account management
timeline.long_term: 18-36 months: Expansion of digital products to include loan applications, investment platforms, and personalized financial services

affected_entities: All major commercial banks in Tunisia, including Societe Generale de Banque en Tunisie, Banque Internationale Arabe de Tunisie, and Attijari Bank Tunisia
Fintech startups and digital payment companies
Central Bank of Tunisia, responsible for regulating and supervising the banking sector

sector_impacts.increased_competition: Banks will need to invest heavily in digital infrastructure to remain competitive, potentially leading to increased costs and reduced profit margins
sector_impacts.improved_customer_experience: Digital banking products will provide customers with greater convenience and flexibility, improving overall satisfaction and loyalty
sector_impacts.job_displacement: Automation of certain banking tasks may lead to job displacement for some employees, particularly in traditional branch networks

differential_impacts.BIAT: As a market leader, BIAT is well-positioned to invest in digital banking and maintain its market share.
differential_impacts.BT: BT's strong brand and customer base will help it to adapt to digital banking, but it may face challenges in integrating new systems.
differential_impacts.ATB: ATB's smaller size and limited resources may make it more difficult to invest in digital banking, putting it at risk of falling behind competitors.

metrics.digital_adoption_rate: Percentage of customers using digital banking products and services
metrics.investment_in_digital_infrastructure: Total amount invested by banks in digital infrastructure and fintech partnerships
metrics.customer_satisfaction: Survey-based measure of customer satisfaction with digital banking products and services
metrics.revenue_growth: Year-over-year revenue growth for each bank, compared to industry average

risk_factors: Dependence on internet and mobile penetration
opportunities: Cost savings through reduced branch and ATM networks
New revenue streams from digital services
Improved customer data collection and analysis
indicators: Return on investment (ROI) for digital banking initiatives
Market share of digital banking services
recommended_actions: Invest in cybersecurity measures to protect customer data
Develop a clear digital banking strategy and roadmap
Partner with fintech companies to leverage their expertise
Monitor customer feedback and adjust digital services accordingly
Continuously assess and improve digital banking infrastructure

differential_impacts.ATB: Lower impact, with potential opportunities for growth through diversification

Improved customer experience through streamlined processes
recommended_actions: Closely monitor regulatory developments and engage with policymakers
Conduct thorough impact assessments and develop contingency plans
Invest in digital transformation and innovation to reduce costs and enhance customer experience
Diversify revenue streams and improve risk management practices
